newsitem.title: ITALY: Montell plans $800 mln investments in 1997,'98.
newsitem.headline: Montell plans $800 mln investments in 1997,'98.

text.p: Montell Polyolefins NV, the world's largest polypropylene producer and a 50/50 joint venture between Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Italy's Montedison SpA , plans to invest $800 million in the next two years.
This would be in addition to the $320-330 million invested in 1996, chief executive Peter Vogtlaender told a meeting of analysts here.

"Montell strategies envisage a reinforcement of its technological and market leadership in Europe and North America, concentrating resources in the higher added value sectors and exploiting the synergies deriving from the merger," he said.
He added that the economic benefit of the synergies already carried out could be quantified at around $45 million for 1996 and would reach $150 million in the year 2000.
Montell, founded in April 1995, had a difficult year that year, but saw a considerable improvement in margins in the first nine months of 1996.
It posted third quarter 1996 operating profit of $101 million against a year-ago $61 million.
In 1997, monomer/polymer spread, or the difference between the price of the raw material, propylene, and polypropylene could narrow after an improvement already seen in 1996, Vogtlaender said.
This would be balanced by the fact that "our break-even point is coming down in a significant way, thanks to cost cutting and better use of productive capacity," he said.
Montell had no plans to build new plants in Europe apart from an installation in the south of France, but a new plant for a new product would be opened in Saudi Arabia, he said without elaborating.

Montedison managing director Enrico Bondi told reporters attending the meeting that the weight of chemicals within the group would increase slightly in 1996 compared to the level of 25 percent of total group turnover in 1995. This would be achieved "by expanding existing productive potential," he said.
